headline: Weekend edition: the week closed soft-dollar — DXY 101.61, first weekly loss in five — with October locked as a hold into the Fed blackout and December the live debate. Friday evening added a tariff cannon (the Graham Act EO: armed, unfired, Oct 18 tripwire), a confirmed Hormuz tanker strike, and Trump's 'more time' on Iran. WTI $100.71, Brent $109.28, spread ~$10.7.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Fed went silent into Saturday's blackout with October locked as a hold (~85%); Friday evening's new wire was trade, not rates — Trump signed the Graham Act EO, a tariff cannon aimed at Russian oil, armed but unfired with an Oct 18 tripwire.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Friday evening's news was trade, not rates. Trump signed the EO implementing the Graham Act (published 7:34pm CT): +500% ad valorem duty on Russian goods, +100% on goods from the top five importers of Russian crude and gas for new purchases made on or after Oct 18, 2026, and +100% on the top five facilitators of Russian-oil sanctions evasion — but Section 4 waives ALL of it under a national-interest certification to Congress. Armed, unfired; Sunday Oct 18 is the tripwire. On rates, the week ended where Thursday left it: October priced as a hold (~85% per Reuters' Friday wire), December the live debate. Goolsbee's 5pm CT Bloomberg interview — the last scheduled Fed voice — never produced a major-wire write-up; the story went cold into Saturday's blackout. The 10-year closed ~5.09% (5.125% post-data high); DXY 101.61 (-0.42%), first weekly loss in five. Thread: Thursday's edition said the market ignored the hot PPI and the October question was about the calendar, not the data; Friday's hot import prices (+1.1%, +8.1% y/y) and the IP beat (+0.7%) couldn't re-arm the hike either — three hot prints, three shrugs, and the dollar fell anyway. What it means: confirms — the October debate is over; the market has moved on to December and to the tariff wildcard. The four-beat read on the EO: (1) it's a sanctions-tariff hybrid — up to +500% duties on Russian goods, +100% on countries still buying Russian oil; (2) the surprise is the waiver — everything is suspended under certification, so it's leverage today, not impact; (3) against the benchmark of revenue actually collected, this is $0 — a threat with a Sunday trigger; (4) for the dollar, tariff threats lean dollar-positive (haven bid plus a terms-of-trade tilt toward the US), but a waived threat is noise — the one-question lens: does Oct 18 bring enforcement or an extended waiver?
chapters.fx: What to watch: blackout now — no Fed voices until Oct 27-28. Weekend: the Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire (enforcement vs waiver extension) and oil's Sunday open. Next week: China Q3 GDP (Mon), Canada CPI (Mon), US housing starts (Tue), UK CPI (Wed), NZ CPI (Wed); FOMC Oct 27-28 is the next focus event.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: Quiet weekend: EUR/USD closed Friday at ~1.1255-1.1259 (+0.33%) — first weekly gain in five-plus — on the dollar fade, not euro strength. The pair still trades the Fed leg; the ECB leg is December (100% priced; October is not a hike).
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing since Friday's close — no new euro driver. Thread: Friday's edition said the two-day rebound ran on dollar weakness (the euro gained less than sterling or the aussie; EUR/GBP fell to 0.8421) and corrected the policy read — October 29 is not priced as a hike; December is 100% with at least one more by April. What it means: thesis stands. The euro's rebound is borrowed momentum — it works only while US yields keep falling (the 170bp US-German gap is the weight). What would change it: a weekend risk shock (euro gives back the fade) or next week's data repricing December.
chapters.fx: What to watch: France's revenue-section vote Oct 20 and Moody's Oct 23 (OAT-Bund 135.2bp); the US 10Y–Bund spread — 10Y toward 5.00% gives the euro room, back over 5.20% kills the rebound.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: Quiet: AUD/USD ~0.695 on Friday's risk rebound — not on Australia. The domestic texture is still the jobs miss (-39.3K, unemployment 4.7%); Kent speaks Saturday evening, readout Sunday.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing since Friday's close. Thread: Friday's edition said the positioning lens flipped — hedge funds are net long AUD at the 79th percentile, which broke the squeeze story; under the contrarian rule, stretched longs mean the pain trade is down, not up, so Friday's rally is rented, not owned. What it means: thesis stands — the aussie rallies on risk while funds sit long; a risk wobble unwinds fast. What would change it: Kent's Saturday-evening remarks (readout Sunday) or China Q3 GDP Monday — the aussie's real fundamentals.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Friday evening confirmed the campaign is still running: India named the MT ST 3 tanker hit by a projectile in Hormuz on Oct 16, Trump gave Iran negotiators 'more time' (no strike decision), and the Graham Act's Russia-oil tariff cannon is armed with an Oct 18 tripwire. WTI $100.71, Brent $109.28, spread ~$10.7.
chapters.meaning: What changed: three Friday-evening items. (1) India's shipping ministry confirmed the crude tanker MT ST 3 was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 16 (15 Indian seafarers safe) — the first named-vessel confirmation beyond the Iranian single-attribution chain; separately, the chemical tanker YARA J was hit by a drone off Romania on Oct 14 (9 safe). (2) Trump Friday (AP): 'not happy' with the Geneva round, no final strike decision, more time for negotiators — zero enrichment remains the red line; the US Embassy in Jerusalem went to authorized departure for nonessential staff; Rubio visits Israel Monday-Tuesday; Vienna technical talks next week. (3) The Graham Act EO: +500% on Russian goods, +100% on the top five Russian-oil buyers for purchases on/after Oct 18 — all waived for now (Sec. 4). Thread: Friday's edition said Ukraine's renewed refinery strikes sent Nov WTI +2.8% to $100.71 (first close over $100 in a month) and Dec Brent +3.2% to $109.28 — escalation winning the day, spread ~$10.7. What it means: confirms and extends — the campaign is broadening (named vessel in Hormuz, drone off Romania) while the diplomacy clock stretches (more time, Vienna next week). The market prices this as a campaign, not a closure. The four-beat read on the ~$10.7 spread: (1) it's what the world pays over the US price for seaborne crude; (2) near the wide end — the premium for shipping risk; (3) a wide spread means the market prices tankers, not demand — the risk lives in the strait; (4) for FX, the spread is the CAD-vs-JPY/EUR tell in one number — wide favors the exporter, taxes the importers. Held, not priced: an uncorroborated Iranian claim of a mine-hit tanker circulated Saturday with no vessel name and no UKMTO confirmation — single-attribution, not in the price.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire (enforcement vs waiver extension) and oil's Sunday open; any new verified Hormuz incident; whether Kyiv heeds the Starshield pressure; Kpler flows (68% of baseline).
